findings.reason: index.ts:29 now returns `hours! * 60 + (minutes || 0)`, so "-03:30" (America/St_Johns) gives -180+30 = -150 instead of -210. The removed line subtracted the minutes when hours was not positive. The wrong value is also stored in the module-level offsetCache, so every later lookup of that string gets it too.
findings.claim: Negative UTC offsets that include minutes (e.g. -03:30) are now computed wrong because the minutes are added to the negative hours instead of subtracted.
findings.evidence: The new line is `return (offsetCache[offsetStr] = hours! * 60 + (minutes || 0));`. For America/St_Johns in winter, Intl longOffset gives "-03:30", so hours=-3 and minutes=30, and the function returns -180+30 = -150 instead of -210. For America/Caracas before 2016 ("-04:30") it returns -210 instead of -270. For Pacific/Marquesas ("-09:30") it returns -510 instead of -570. The removed line `hours > 0 ? hours * 60 + minutes : hours * 60 - minutes` handled the sign correctly. The wrong value is also stored in the module-level `offsetCache`, so every later call with that offset string gets it too.

findings.reason: `"-00:25".split(":").map(Number)` gives [-0, 25], and the new line computes -0*60 + 25 = 25. The old code took the `hours > 0` false branch and returned -25. Lowered from high to medium because only historical LMT-style offsets like Europe/Dublin before 1880 hit this.
findings.claim: Offsets between -00:01 and -00:59 come out positive because Number("-00") is -0 and the sign is lost when the minutes are added.
findings.evidence: For offsetStr "-00:25:21", `split(":").map(Number)` gives [-0, 25, 21], and `-0*60 + 25` = 25 instead of -25. The old code took the `hours > 0` false branch and computed `-0*60 - 25` = -25. The new code also drops the seconds part, but so did the old code.

findings.reason: In tests.ts the only negative zone is America/New_York (-300) and the only fractional zone is Asia/Kathmandu (+345), so the new formula passes every test. Lowered to low because this is a coverage gap in the locked baseline tests, not a defect the change adds; the real bug is the C1/X1 item.
findings.claim: The locked tests have no negative fractional offset, so the sign regression passes the suite.
findings.evidence: The only negative zone in the tests is America/New_York (-5*60). The only fractional zone is Asia/Kathmandu (+345), which is positive. No test covers America/St_Johns, Pacific/Marquesas or any other "-HH:30" or "-HH:45" offset. Under the new formula these tests pass while a negative fractional offset gives the wrong result.

findings.reason: String.split always returns at least one element, so `hours` can never be undefined at runtime. The removed guard was dead code, and dropping it changes no behaviour.
findings.claim: The undefined guard was replaced with a non-null assertion.
findings.evidence: The removed lines were `// type-guard if (hours === undefined) { return NaN; }`. The new code relies on `hours!`. Nothing breaks at runtime, because split always returns at least one element, but it is a type-check suppression added in place of a guard.
